statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-119079 is a denial of service in the krb5 ASN.1 decoder: decode_sequence_of() in src/lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c grows the decoded array one element at a time, so an unauthenticated attacker who sends a protocol message containing a very long ASN.1 sequence can make the KDC or an application server spend a large amount of CPU time decoding it. MIT fixed it in krb5 1.22.3, announced at https://mailman.mit.edu/pipermail/kerberos-announce/2026q4/000212.html, with commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/205832663330da308d9d031a17326b68a16715fd on the krb5-1.22 branch, contained in the krb5-1.22.3-final tag and not in krb5-1.22.2-final; it changes only asn1_encode.c, making decode_sequence_of() count and validate the elements first so the array is allocated once, and its message names this CVE. Alpine's krb5 1.22.3-r0 on the 3.23-stable branch upgrades to MIT 1.22.3 and lists CVE-2026-119079 under 1.22.3-r0 in its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/2cb5928755d78bc5381941f16adedf76bfbcde96/main/krb5/APKBUILD. The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository (main and security, x86_64 and aarch64) publishes packages built from source krb5 at 1.22.1-r0 and 1.22.3-r0 (plus krb5-conf 1.0-r2, which holds only configuration). The libkrb5 library in the krb5-libs package reports krb5-1.22.3-final in the 1.22.3-r0 build and krb5-1.22.1-final in 1.22.1-r0, on both architectures, each package verified against its index checksum. 1.22.1-r0 is MIT 1.22.1, which predates the fix, so it is affected; the range ends at 1.22.3-r0, the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-119079 is a denial of service in the krb5 ASN.1 decoder: decode_sequence_of() in src/lib/krb5/asn.1/asn1_encode.c grows the decoded array one element at a time, so an unauthenticated attacker who sends a protocol message containing a very long ASN.1 sequence can make the KDC or an application server spend a large amount of CPU time decoding it. MIT fixed it in krb5 1.22.3, announced at https://mailman.mit.edu/pipermail/kerberos-announce/2026q4/000212.html, with commit https://github.com/krb5/krb5/commit/205832663330da308d9d031a17326b68a16715fd on the krb5-1.22 branch, contained in the krb5-1.22.3-final tag and not in krb5-1.22.2-final; it changes only asn1_encode.c, making decode_sequence_of() count and validate the elements first so the array is allocated once, and its message names this CVE. Debian fixed it for trixie in 1.21.3-5+deb13u2 (DSA-6650-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-119079. The DHI Debian repository publishes three rebuilds of Debian's 1.21.3-5+deb13u1 and one rebuild of Debian's fixed 1.21.3-5+deb13u2. We checked every binary package of these four builds, including libgssrpc4t64, libkrb5-3 and the libkrb5-dbg debug symbols, for amd64 and arm64, each verified against its index checksum, with function sizes read from the debug symbols: the third rebuild's decode_sequence_of() in libkrb5.so.3.3, which the fix rewrites, is 652 bytes on amd64 and 580 on arm64, against 433 and 444 in the first two rebuilds, and its package changelog records the backport of this fix. In the rebuild of 1.21.3-5+deb13u2 decode_sequence_of() has the same fixed size (652 and 580 bytes), and its changelog lists this CVE. The range ends at the third rebuild of 1.21.3-5+deb13u1, the first published build with the fix; the later rebuild of 1.21.3-5+deb13u2 also carries it.
